notes: ASSERTION DESIGN ISSUE: The only failing assertion ('Decomposes into 2-4 separate issues') was too restrictive. The with_skill version produced 5 well-bounded issues (separating email delivery from preferences), which is arguably better decomposition than the baseline's 4 issues (which combined email+preferences). Consider widening to '3-6 issues' in future iterations.

NON-DISCRIMINATING ASSERTIONS: Evals 1 and 2 show 100% pass for both configurations. The JTBD template format is well-known enough that baseline Claude produces high-quality issues even without the skill. The skill's value is more qualitative (coaching behavior, fewer questions, assumption-first approach) than captured by structural assertions.

QUALITATIVE DIFFERENCES (not captured by assertions): (1) With-skill asked 2-3 targeted questions vs baseline's 5-6; (2) With-skill led with assumptions+draft vs baseline leading with questions; (3) With-skill included --label ready-for-spec consistently, baseline missed it in eval 1; (4) With-skill included refinement paths showing how the issue would evolve based on different user responses.

TIME/TOKEN TRADEOFF: With-skill averaged 27s longer and 1600 more tokens. This is expected — the skill adds methodology context. For issue-craft, the time overhead is modest relative to the human time saved on issue quality.
